t: Universal Relationship Explorer: a plain-language overview
title: Universal Relationship Explorer: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Universal Relationship Explorer does and why archives need it. A universal relationship explorer lets you walk the archive's web of connections: start at any record and follow its links — cites, derived-from, same-as, mentions — hop by hop, with every path explained in plain words. It is a guided tour of how everything connects to everything.
demo:
# Universal Relationship Explorer - runnable demo (JAH-ATK200-000001)
from collections import deque, defaultdict
RANK = 1
SIG = False
EDGES = [('archive-1', 'cites', 'paper-2'), ('paper-2', 'derived-from', 'dataset-5'), ('archive-1', 'mentions', 'person-9'), ('dataset-5', 'same-as', 'dataset-5b')]  # (a, rel, b)
START, MAXHOPS = "archive-1", 3
adj = defaultdict(list)
for a, rel, b in EDGES:
    adj[a].append((rel, b)); adj[b].append(("rev:" + rel, a))
paths = {START: []}
q = deque([(START, 0)])
while q:
    node, d = q.popleft()
    if d >= MAXHOPS: continue
    for rel, nb in adj[node]:
        if nb not in paths:
            paths[nb] = paths[node] + [(node, rel, nb)]
            q.append((nb, d+1))
print("exploring from %s (max %d hops): reached %d nodes" % (START, MAXHOPS, len(paths)-1))
for node, p in paths.items():
    if not p: continue
    expl = " -> ".join("%s -[%s]-> %s" % (a, rel, b) for a, rel, b in p)
    print(" ", expl)
    if RANK < 2: break
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("edge types seen:", dict(Counter(rel for _, rel, _ in EDGES)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-EXP-" + "JAH-ATK200-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK200-000001", "OK")
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Universal Relationship Explorer works

t: How the Universal Relationship Explorer works: the deep tour
title: How the Universal Relationship Explorer works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Universal Relationship Explorer does and why archives need it. Real explorers run graph traversals (BFS/DFS) from a start node over typed edges, filter by relationship type and strength, and explain each discovered path ('A cites B which was derived from C'). Neighborhood inspection summarizes a node's connections by type, shortest-path queries answer 'how are X and Y connected?', and traversal budgets (max hops, max nodes) keep exploration bounded. Every path shown carries its edge evidence. Advanced explorers rank paths by interestingness (rare edge types, strong links), detect meaningful multi-hop patterns (A and B share three independent connections), and let users save exploration trails as shareable investigations. Quality is measured by path-explanation clarity ratings and query latency on large graphs. The limits are hairball neighborhoods where everything connects to everything — the explorer filters by strength and type rather than dumping the whole graph, because an unfiltered dump explains nothing.

It is a guided tour of how everything connects to everything.
demo:
# Universal Relationship Explorer - runnable demo (JAH-ATK200-000013)
from collections import deque, defaultdict
RANK = 1
SIG = False
EDGES = [('archive-1', 'cites', 'paper-2'), ('paper-2', 'derived-from', 'dataset-5'), ('archive-1', 'mentions', 'person-9'), ('dataset-5', 'same-as', 'dataset-5b')]  # (a, rel, b)
START, MAXHOPS = "archive-1", 3
adj = defaultdict(list)
for a, rel, b in EDGES:
    adj[a].append((rel, b)); adj[b].append(("rev:" + rel, a))
paths = {START: []}
q = deque([(START, 0)])
while q:
    node, d = q.popleft()
    if d >= MAXHOPS: continue
    for rel, nb in adj[node]:
        if nb not in paths:
            paths[nb] = paths[node] + [(node, rel, nb)]
            q.append((nb, d+1))
print("exploring from %s (max %d hops): reached %d nodes" % (START, MAXHOPS, len(paths)-1))
for node, p in paths.items():
    if not p: continue
    expl = " -> ".join("%s -[%s]-> %s" % (a, rel, b) for a, rel, b in p)
    print(" ", expl)
    if RANK < 2: break
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("edge types seen:", dict(Counter(rel for _, rel, _ in EDGES)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-EXP-" + "JAH-ATK200-000013")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK200-000013", "OK")

Real explorers run graph traversals (BFS/DFS) from a start node over typed edges, filter by relationship type and strength, and explain each discovered path ('A cites B which was derived from C'). Neighborhood inspection summarizes a node's connections by type, shortest-path queries answer 'how are X and Y connected?', and traversal budgets (max hops, max nodes) keep exploration bounded. Every path shown carries its edge evidence.

title: The Universal Relationship Explorer at archive scale
description: Production: how the Universal Relationship Explorer runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real explorers run graph traversals (BFS/DFS) from a start node over typed edges, filter by relationship type and strength, and explain each discovered path ('A cites B which was derived from C'). Neighborhood inspection summarizes a node's connections by type, shortest-path queries answer 'how are X and Y connected?', and traversal budgets (max hops, max nodes) keep exploration bounded. Every path shown carries its edge evidence. Advanced explorers rank paths by interestingness (rare edge types, strong links), detect meaningful multi-hop patterns (A and B share three independent connections), and let users save exploration trails as shareable investigations. Quality is measured by path-explanation clarity ratings and query latency on large graphs. The limits are hairball neighborhoods where everything connects to everything — the explorer filters by strength and type rather than dumping the whole graph, because an unfiltered dump explains nothing.
